summary: In the house, Jesus explains the parable of the tares: He sows the good seed, the devil sows the bad, and His angels will separate them at the end.
key_insight: Jesus begins and ends the explanation with Himself. The Son of Man sows the good seed, and the Son of Man sends out His angels at the harvest to clear “His kingdom.” The One who plants His people is the One who will judge.
story: Then Jesus sent the crowds away and went into the house. His disciples came to Him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the tares of the field.”

He answered, “He who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.” The field is the world. The good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, and the tares are the sons of the wicked one. The enemy who sowed them is the devil, the harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are the angels.

Just as the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of this age. “The Son of Man will send out His angels, and they will gather out of His kingdom all things that offend, and those who practice lawlessness,” and they will cast them into the furnace of fire, where there will be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
“Then the righteous will shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”

scene.label: The house
scene.text: Matthew 13 began with Jesus leaving the house to teach by the sea (13:1), and now He returns to it (13:36). This was probably the home in Capernaum where He stayed, perhaps Peter’s.

scene.label: The furnace of fire
scene.text: Every Jew knew the story of Nebuchadnezzar’s burning fiery furnace (Daniel 3). In the Psalms, the wicked gnash their teeth in bitter rage (Psalm 112:10). Jesus joins these images to describe final judgment.

scene.label: Shining like the sun
scene.text: Jesus’ promise echoes Daniel 12:3: “Those who are wise shall shine Like the brightness of the firmament.” The verse before it is the Old Testament’s clearest promise of resurrection (Daniel 12:2).

scene.label: “His angels”
scene.text: In Daniel 7:13–14 one like the Son of Man receives an everlasting kingdom. Jesus speaks of “His angels” and “His kingdom,” claiming that royal authority as His own.

witnesses.matthew: Only Matthew records the explanation, and he sets it in private, after the crowds have gone, just as Mark says Jesus explained everything to His disciples alone (Mark 4:34). Matthew’s Gospel returns often to the final separation of good and evil, and this is one of its clearest pictures.

seeing.reveals: Jesus speaks with calm authority about the end of history. He names the devil as the enemy and the angels as His servants, and He promises that His people will shine like the sun.
seeing.living: The field is the world, so expect wheat and tares to grow side by side until the end. Live as “sons of the kingdom” without despair or panic, because the Son of Man will finish what He started, and those who belong to Him will shine.
seeing.ponder: When you think about the end of the age, do you feel dread, or the hope of shining in your Father’s kingdom, and why?

preaching.big_idea: The Son of Man who sowed His people in the world will gather them into glory.
preaching.watch_for: Jesus says “the field is the world” (v. 38), yet the angels gather offenders “out of His kingdom” (v. 41). Some apply the parable to false believers within the church; others to the world at large, noting that Jesus elsewhere commands church discipline (Matthew 18:15–17). Either way, the final separation belongs to the Son of Man and His angels.
